title: House Robber II
prompt:
Same as House Robber, but the houses are arranged in a **circle**, so the first and last houses are adjacent. Return the maximum you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.

**Example**: `[2,3,2]` → `3` (houses 0 and 2 are neighbors, so you can't take both 2s).

**Constraints**: `1 <= nums.length <= 100`, `0 <= nums[i] <= 1000`.
hints: The circle adds exactly one new conflict. Which two houses, and can you ever rob both?
Any valid plan skips the first house or skips the last house (or both). Each case is an ordinary straight-line street.
`Math.max(robLine(nums, 0, n - 2), robLine(nums, 1, n - 1))`, with `n == 1` handled separately.

solution.explanation: Since house 0 and house n-1 can't both be robbed, every valid plan fits inside [0..n-2] or [1..n-1]. Solving both straight lines and taking the max covers every plan exactly. A single house has no range to split, so it's returned directly. O(n) time, O(1) space.
